marrow__ANAT_CH53_Q015.takeaway: Colles' membranous superficial perineal fascia attaches to the perineal membrane and ischiopubic rami, limiting urine spread into the thigh and anal triangle.
marrow__ANAT_CH53_Q015.displayText:
Colles' membranous superficial perineal fascia attaches to the perineal membrane and ischiopubic rami, limiting urine spread into the thigh and anal triangle.

Colles' fascia prevents extravasated urine from spreading into the thigh and anal triangle.

Scarpa's fascia is continuous with the superficial fascia of the scrotum and becomes Colles' fascia in the perineum. In women it continues into the labia majora and perineal fascia.

Colles' fascia attaches posteriorly to the perineal membrane, preventing fluid spread into the anal triangle, and laterally to the ischiopubic rami and fascia lata along Holden's line, preventing spread into the thigh.

Camper's fascia is the superficial fatty layer of abdominal superficial fascia; Scarpa's fascia is its deep membranous layer; Buck's fascia is the deep fascia of the penis.

Clinical significance: with urethral rupture, urine may extravasate into the superficial perineal pouch, penis, scrotum/labia majora, and anterior abdominal wall.
emphasis: Colles' membranous superficial perineal fascia attaches to the perineal membrane and ischiopubic rami, limiting urine spread into the thigh and anal triangle

rationales.a: Camper's fatty layer is superficial abdominal fascia and does not provide the key posterior/lateral perineal attachments.
rationales.b: Scarpa's membranous layer continues into the perineum as Colles' fascia; the named attachment at the pouch is Colles' fascia itself.
rationales.c: Buck's fascia is deep fascia around the penis and does not form the superficial pouch boundary that restricts urine spread.

marrow__ANAT_CH53_Q016.takeaway: The bulbourethral glands lie in the deep perineal pouch; the superficial pouch contains external-genital roots, superficial muscles and related structures.
marrow__ANAT_CH53_Q016.displayText:
The bulbourethral glands lie in the deep perineal pouch; the superficial pouch contains external-genital roots, superficial muscles and related structures.

Bulbourethral glands are not a content of the superficial perineal pouch; they are in the deep perineal pouch.

The superficial perineal pouch is the potential space between the perineal membrane above and Colles' fascia below. Its contents differ in males and females and include the roots of the external genitalia, superficial perineal muscles, and related neurovascular structures.
emphasis: The bulbourethral glands lie in the deep perineal pouch; the superficial pouch contains external-genital roots, superficial muscles and related structures

rationales.a: The root of the penis lies in the superficial perineal pouch, so it is not the excluded structure.
rationales.b: Bulbospongiosus is a superficial perineal muscle and lies in the superficial pouch.
rationales.c: Greater vestibular glands lie in the superficial perineal pouch in females.

marrow__ANAT_CH53_Q017.takeaway: The root of the penis lies in the superficial perineal pouch; the deep pouch includes the urethral sphincter, bulbourethral glands and dorsal nerve.
marrow__ANAT_CH53_Q017.displayText:
The root of the penis lies in the superficial perineal pouch; the deep pouch includes the urethral sphincter, bulbourethral glands and dorsal nerve.

The root of the penis is not a content of the deep perineal pouch; it lies in the superficial perineal pouch.

The deep perineal pouch lies between the endopelvic fascia and the perineal membrane. Contents listed include dorsal nerve of penis/clitoris, deep transverse perineal muscle, sphincter urethrae, penile/clitoral artery branches, urethral structures, and bulbourethral glands in males.
emphasis: The root of the penis lies in the superficial perineal pouch; the deep pouch includes the urethral sphincter, bulbourethral glands and dorsal nerve

rationales.a: The dorsal nerve of the penis passes through the deep perineal pouch and accompanies the pudendal neurovascular structures.
rationales.b: Bulbourethral glands lie in the deep perineal pouch beside the membranous urethra.
rationales.d: Sphincter urethrae is a deep perineal muscle surrounding the membranous urethra.

marrow__ANAT_CH53_Q018.takeaway: The internal anal sphincter is smooth muscle and is not an attachment to the perineal body; bulbospongiosus and transverse perineal muscles attach there.
marrow__ANAT_CH53_Q018.displayText:
The internal anal sphincter is smooth muscle and is not an attachment to the perineal body; bulbospongiosus and transverse perineal muscles attach there.

The internal anal sphincter is not involved in formation of the perineal body.

The perineal body is a fibromuscular structure in the midline at the junction of the anal and urogenital triangles. Muscular attachments include anteriorly superficial and deep transverse perineal muscles and bulbospongiosus; posteriorly the external anal sphincter; superiorly puborectalis, pubovaginalis, and the rectovaginal septum.

It is continuous with the perineal membrane and superficial perineal fascia. In males it continues as the perineal raphe; in females it attaches to the posterior commissure and introitus.
emphasis: The internal anal sphincter is smooth muscle and is not an attachment to the perineal body; bulbospongiosus and transverse perineal muscles attach there

rationales.a: Bulbospongiosus attaches to the perineal body and contributes to its anterior muscular connections.
rationales.b: The superficial transverse perineal muscles attach to and stabilize the perineal body.
rationales.c: Deep transverse perineal fibers contribute to the perineal body's muscular support.

marrow__ANAT_CH53_Q019.takeaway: Obturator internus and its fascia form the lateral wall of the ischioanal fossa; the medial wall is the anal sphincter and levator ani.
marrow__ANAT_CH53_Q019.displayText:
Obturator internus and its fascia form the lateral wall of the ischioanal fossa; the medial wall is the anal sphincter and levator ani.

The lateral boundary of the ischioanal fossa is formed by obturator internus with its fascia.

The ischioanal fossa is a wedge-shaped fat-filled space on either side of the anal canal. Boundaries: anterior — posterior border of perineal membrane; posterior — gluteus maximus and sacrotuberous ligament; lateral — ischial tuberosity and obturator internus; medial — external anal sphincter and pelvic diaphragm (levator ani).

Clinical significance: the ischioanal fossa provides a relatively bloodless surgical plane during resection of anal cancers.
emphasis: Obturator internus and its fascia form the lateral wall of the ischioanal fossa; the medial wall is the anal sphincter and levator ani

rationales.a: The perineal membrane forms the anterior boundary of the fossa, not its posterior boundary.
rationales.b: The sacrotuberous ligament contributes posteriorly with gluteus maximus rather than forming the anterior boundary.
rationales.d: Gluteus maximus lies posteriorly; the medial boundary is external anal sphincter and pelvic diaphragm.

marrow__ANAT_CH53_Q020.takeaway: Alcock's pudendal canal is a fascial tunnel in the obturator internus fascia carrying the pudendal nerve and internal pudendal vessels.
marrow__ANAT_CH53_Q020.displayText:
Alcock's pudendal canal is a fascial tunnel in the obturator internus fascia carrying the pudendal nerve and internal pudendal vessels.

Alcock's (pudendal) canal is formed by the fascia of the obturator internus muscle.

It is created by connective tissue binding the internal pudendal vessels and pudendal nerve to the medial surface of obturator internus fascia.

Contents: internal pudendal artery and pudendal nerve.

Clinical significance: pudendal nerve block at the ischial spine can provide analgesia to the lower vagina, posterior perineum, and vulva; pudendal neuralgia may result from nerve compression in the canal.
emphasis: Alcock's pudendal canal is a fascial tunnel in the obturator internus fascia carrying the pudendal nerve and internal pudendal vessels

rationales.a: Levator ani forms the pelvic floor and does not provide the fascia enclosing the pudendal canal.
rationales.c: External anal sphincter surrounds the anal canal but does not form the lateral-wall canal that transmits pudendal structures.
rationales.d: Gluteus minimus is a hip abductor and is unrelated to the obturator fascia tunnel.
